title: Mastercard unveils Agent Pay with registered agents and Agentic Tokens
summary: Mastercard announced Agent Pay, an agentic payments program in which AI agents must be registered and verified before they can pay on a consumer's behalf, consumers control what an agent is allowed to purchase, and payments run on Agentic Tokens that extend Mastercard's existing tokenization so participants across the value chain can recognize agent-initiated transactions. Mastercard named Microsoft (Azure OpenAI Service and Copilot Studio), IBM (watsonx Orchestrate for B2B), Braintree and Checkout.com as partners, and said it would add merchant interfaces to distinguish trusted agents from bad actors and a process to clarify agentic transactions that are unfamiliar or unrecognized.

actors.deployer: Microsoft (Copilot Studio, Azure OpenAI Service); IBM (watsonx Orchestrate)

verification_note: URL fetched 2026-10-17; the page is dated April 29, 2025 and its headline matches the claim. Agent registration and verification, consumer control over what the agent may purchase, Agentic Tokens built on existing tokenization, the four named partners and the process for unrecognized agentic transactions are all stated on the page. The mechanisms are described in prospective language (agents 'will be required to be registered and verified'); the page reports no live transaction and no rollout date.
